title: Evolution from an acoustic-plasmon-mediated superconductivity to an acoustic-phonon-mediated superconductivity in bilayers
authors: Shuyang Wang, Sankar Das Sarma, Jay D. Sau
abstract: Motivated by recent developments in van der Waals heterostructures, we revisit the acoustic plasmon mechanism of superconductivity in bilayer systems composed of a light layer (LL) and heavy layer (HL) by employing Eliashberg theory. The exchange of virtual plasmons in the HL can lead to a retarded in time attractive interaction between electrons of LL that we model through the screened interaction in the bilayer system within the random phase approximation. We explore the evolution from acoustic plasmon mediated superconductivity to phonon mediated superconductivity by studying the evolution of $T_c$ as the HL mass is increased by a few orders of magnitude compared with the electronic mass in LL. The lower HL mass corresponds to the bilayer acoustic plasmon, while the latter regime is closer to the Born-Oppenheimer regime of acoustic phonon mediated strongly retarded pairing. The heavy HL mass limit is known to obey Migdal's theorem by virtue of the small ratio of the two individual layer masses. We study the nonadiabatic effects for the arbitrary mass ratio with no small parameter systematically by using a frequency cut off in the Eliashberg theory, providing $T_c$ as a function of this cut off.
summary: This work theoretically examines how superconductivity emerges in bilayer heterostructures as a function of layer mass contrast. By applying Eliashberg theory, the authors demonstrate a continuous crossover from plasmon-mediated pairing (low mass ratio) to phonon-like pairing (high mass ratio). The study suggests that SC might be robustly present across this entire parameter space.
main_problem: The study investigates the mechanism of superconductivity in bilayer van der Waals heterostructures, specifically tracking the crossover from acoustic plasmon-mediated pairing to acoustic phonon-mediated pairing.
main_result: Superconductivity is predicted to exist continuously as the mass ratio between the two layers ($m_2/m_1$) is tuned, suggesting that SC may be a generic feature in bilayers with large mass differences.
method: The analysis employs Eliashberg theory combined with calculations of the dynamically screened Coulomb interaction derived within the Random Phase Approximation (RPA).
model_or_system: The model consists of a bilayer system comprising two 2D electron gases: a light layer (LL) and a heavy layer (HL), whose coupling mediates the pairing interaction.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), which is studied as a function of various physical parameters.
important_parameters: The mass ratio ($m_2/m_1$) is the primary tuning parameter, alongside carrier densities and an artificial frequency cut-off ($\omega_c$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include using RPA for screening and introducing a frequency cut-off ($\omega_c$) to handle divergences in Eliashberg theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $\log_{10}(T_c)$ on density and mass ratio, showing trends across different fixed values of the frequency cut-off.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the pairing interaction derived from acoustic plasmons using RPA, applies this to the linearized Eliashberg equation, and then maps out the continuous crossover behavior by varying the layer mass ratio $m_2/m_1$.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity mechanisms, the systematic theoretical framework for analyzing pairing mediated by collective excitations (plasmons vs. phonons) in layered systems is relevant to understanding strongly correlated electron physics and emergent quantum phenomena.
